title.narrative: Rural Access and Agricultural Marketing Project - Scale Up

description.narrative: The Rural Access and Agricultural Marketing Project (RAAMP) Scale Up (SU) continues and expands support provided under the series of rural road access projects in Nigeria, leveraging the previously supported rural road asset management and its institutional framework. The project will scale-up support provided to the rural connectivity agenda in the country through the Rural Access and Mobility Project Phase 1 RAMP-1 (P072644), the Second Rural Access and Mobility programs or RAMP-2 (P095003), and the ongoing Nigeria Rural Access and Agricultural Marketing Project (P163353) financed by the World Bank and the Agence Française de Developpement (AFD), as well as the Nigeria Access to Agri Markets project, recently approved by European investment Bank (EIB).The RAAMP SU Project consists of three mutually reinforcing components to support improvements in Nigeria's rural road network. The first will support direct rehabilitation and upgrades of 3000 km of resilient rural roads, integrating road safety consideration, and building climate resilience. The second will support climate resilient asset management, including supporting operations and maintenance of an additional 3500 km of rural roads and a climate-risk informed road asset management system. Finally, the third component will support institutional transformation and project management. Project activities also include mechanisms to support road safety management, digitalized outcome monitoring, and skills development for management of rural roads as well as gender-targeted opportunities.All states will be eligible to participate in the RAAMP-SU operation subject to meeting specific criteria to demonstrate the state's commitment to institutional reforms and sustainable financing. Candidate roads from participating states will be assessed according to economic, social, and climate vulnerability criteria as part of the selection and prioritization process. As with the preceding RAAMP project, the Federal Ministry of Agriculture and Food Security will continue to be the project federal counterpart, ensuring project implementation at the federal level through an entity to be created within the newly established National Agriculture Development Fund. State rural access road agencies will be responsible for project implementation at the state level.

The project objective is to improve rural access and climate resilience of communities in targeted rural areas and strengthen institutional capacity for management of the rural road network and in case of an Eligible Crisis or Emergency, respond promptly or effectively to it.

title.narrative: Rural Road Sector Reforms adopted at national level

comment.narrative: Action towards the creation and operationalization of the Rural Roads Directorate under the National Agriculture Development Fund (NADF)

title.narrative: New operational policies and measures adopted by NADF new National Rural Roads Directorate

comment.narrative: Specifically, it tracks whether the National Agricultural Development Fund (NADF) and the newly established National Rural Roads Directorate have formally adopted new operational policies and measures. A "Yes" indicates that these policies and measures are in place, signaling progress in strengthening the institutional framework for rural road development and maintenance, while a "No" suggests that reforms are still pending.
The indicator reflects both physical achievements and the adoption of resilient engineering practices to ensure long-term sustainability and accessibility of rural roads.

title.narrative: Road safety measures and reforms in place and adopted in participating states

comment.narrative: The percentage reflects the proportion of states that have integrated road safety measures into their policies, regulations, and operational frameworks. It serves as a benchmark for tracking progress in institutionalizing road safety reforms, enhancing infrastructure safety, and ensuring compliance with best practices to reduce accidents and improve road user safety.

title.narrative: Climate risk management framework in place and adopted in participating states

comment.narrative: The percentage reflects the proportion of states that have met the required criteria for framework adoption, indicating progress in institutionalizing climate resilience strategies within rural road planning and maintenance

title.narrative: People reporting improved experience with rural connectivity supported by the project

comment.narrative: This assesses the percentage of people who report a positive change in their ability to access essential services (such as markets, healthcare, and education) and economic opportunities due to project interventions

title.narrative: Road sector reforms and measures completed and adopted for RARAs in participating states

comment.narrative: This indicator measures the extent to which road sector reforms and institutional measures for the establishment and operationalization of Rural Access Road Agencies (RARAs) have been completed and formally adopted in participating states. The percentage value reflects progress in enacting legal frameworks, setting up institutional structures, and implementing necessary policies to ensure sustainable rural road management

title.narrative: Beneficiaries of the apprenticeship who report being employed 12 months after completing the program

comment.narrative: This indicator will measure the effectiveness and long-term impact of an apprenticeship program in facilitating employment

title.narrative: Participating states with enhanced climate resilient planning, preparation, surveillance, and/or response

comment.narrative: This will assess the extent to which states have adopted and implemented measures to enhance resilience against climate-related risks in rural road infrastructure and agricultural supply chains. The indicator reflects progress in institutional strengthening, policy adoption, and operational readiness for climate adaptation and disaster risk management within the project framework.

title.narrative: Direct users that benefit from improved access to sustainable transport infrastructure and services

comment.narrative: This will be measured by the project's impact on mobility and accessibility, with a focus on inclusivity by disaggregating data for women and youth.

title.narrative: NiTRiMS integrating climate risks module and operational in all supported states

comment.narrative: This will capture the proportion of supported states where the system is fully functional with the climate risks module, indicating progress in strengthening climate resilience in rural road planning and management.

title.narrative: People benefiting from climate resilient infrastructure

comment.narrative: This will track how the infrastructure investments contribute to improved accessibility, reduced vulnerability to extreme weather events, and overall community well-being. The indicator helps assess the project's impact on enhancing climate resilience at the local level.
